subject: Chemistry
title: Haloarenes by Electrophilic Substitution: Reaction and Mechanism
summary: Aryl chlorides and bromides are made by electrophilic substitution: C₆H₆ + Br₂ → C₆H₅Br + HBr with FeBr₃ (or Fe) in the dark, and Cl₂ / FeCl₃ gives chlorobenzene. FeBr₃ (a Lewis acid) turns Br₂ into the electrophile Br⁺; Br⁺ attacks the ring to form the arenium ion (σ-complex), whose + charge is spread over the ortho and para carbons; loss of H⁺ restores aromaticity and regenerates the catalyst. Iodination needs an oxidising agent (HNO₃ / HIO₄); fluorine is too reactive.

notes.title: Haloarenes by Electrophilic Substitution
notes.blurb: the reaction, the three-step mechanism with the arenium ion, toluene, iodine and fluorine, common mistakes

keyPoints: C₆H₆ + Br₂ → C₆H₅Br + HBr with **FeBr₃ (or Fe), in the dark**; Cl₂ / FeCl₃ gives C₆H₅Cl.
It is **substitution, not addition**: the aromatic ring is kept.
Step 1: **Br₂ + FeBr₃ → Br⁺ + FeBr₄⁻** (FeBr₃ is a Lewis acid).
Step 2: the π electrons attack Br⁺ → **arenium ion (σ-complex)**, + spread over the ortho and para carbons.
Step 3: FeBr₄⁻ removes **H⁺**, the ring is aromatic again and FeBr₃ is regenerated.
Iodination needs **HNO₃ or HIO₄** (removes HI); **fluorine** is too reactive for this method.

blocks.p: **C₆H₆ + Br₂ → C₆H₅Br + HBr** (FeBr₃ or Fe, dark) and **C₆H₆ + Cl₂ → C₆H₅Cl + HCl** (FeCl₃ or Fe, dark). One H of the ring is replaced by the halogen; benzene does not add Br₂ because addition would destroy its aromaticity.

head: Step
What happens
rows: A Br of Br₂ gives a lone pair to Fe; the Br–Br bond breaks with both electrons going to the Br on iron: Br₂ + FeBr₃ → Br⁺ + FeBr₄⁻.

Two π electrons of a ring C=C attack Br⁺; a new C–Br bond forms. The carbon becomes sp³ (H and Br) and the next carbon carries +: the arenium ion (σ-complex). By resonance the + is shared by the two ortho carbons and the para carbon. Aromaticity is lost.
A Br of FeBr₄⁻ removes H⁺ from the sp³ carbon; the C–H electrons re-form the C=C. The ring is aromatic again: C₆H₅Br + HBr, and FeBr₃ is regenerated.

blocks.p: **Toluene** + X₂ (Fe, dark) gives **o- and p-halotoluene** (the CH₃ group directs ortho / para); they are separated by their very different melting points. In light, the halogen goes on the CH₃ side chain instead. **Iodination** is reversible (HI reduces C₆H₅I back), so HNO₃ or HIO₄ is added to oxidise HI. **Fluorine** reacts too violently, so fluoro compounds are not made this way.
